questions: Should the minimum number of operations be counted as the total number of adjacent swaps performed, or can multiple swaps be combined into a single operation?
Is the string indexed from 1 to N in the description, and does the input string S correspond to this 1‑based indexing without any leading spaces or newline characters?
Are there any limits on the size of the answer (e.g., should it fit in a 32‑bit integer, or must we use 64‑bit types)?
Must the output be printed as a plain integer followed by a newline, or are additional spaces or formatting allowed?
If the string already has all 1s contiguous, should the answer be 0, and is this case considered valid input?
Are there any hidden constraints on the number of 1s (e.g., can the string consist entirely of 1s)?
In case of multiple optimal ways to achieve contiguity, does it matter which final segment of 1s is chosen, or only the minimal number of swaps?
Should the program handle extremely large N efficiently (e.g., O(N) time), or are slower solutions acceptable within the time limits?
